content_metadata.description: A tutorial and demonstration on using post-processing techniques to enhance visual fidelity in video games, illustrated with examples from various game footages and a detailed explanation of using Unity's post-processing stack.

qAndA.answer: Enabling 'Is Global' makes the volume's effect apply to the entire scene, regardless of the volume's position or the camera's location within it.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of enabling the 'Is Global' toggle on the Post Process Volume?

qAndA.answer: The narrator suggests cranking up the directional light intensity higher than 1.
qAndA.question: What is the recommended value for the directional light intensity to make the auto-exposure effect work more effectively?

qAndA.answer: Lowering the 'Aperture' value increases the blur in the areas outside of the focus distance, creating a more pronounced depth of field effect.
qAndA.question: What effect does lowering the 'Aperture' value have on the Depth of Field effect?

qAndA.answer: Increasing the 'Shutter Angle' will create a stronger motion blur effect, making moving objects appear more blurred.
qAndA.question: How does the 'Shutter Angle' setting in the Motion Blur effect impact the visual result?

qAndA.answer: The primary goal is to improve the visual fidelity and cinematic quality of the game scene.
qAndA.question: What is the primary goal of the post-processing techniques demonstrated in the video?

youtube_description:
In this video we take a look at how to use the Post-Processing Stack in Unity to drastically improve the look of our visuals in our project.

We take a look at how to get started using post-processing and work to create a realistic auto-exposure effect.

We also take a look at how to use the depth of field effect to create a tilt-shift effect on our camera. 

Be sure to LIKE and SUBSCRIBE if you enjoyed this guide! Share the video for extra love!
